title: Mosaic garter wrap
subtitle: A rectangular DK wrap in two-colour mosaic knitting — slip stitch colourwork, no stranding.
excerpt: A rectangular wrap in DK wool worked in a two-colour mosaic pattern using only slip stitches, never carrying two colours on the same row. Each row uses only one colour; the second colour is slipped and floated without being worked. Finished size approximately 40 cm wide by 170 cm long. About 200 g each of two DK yarns in contrasting values.
sourceNotes: Mosaic knitting (two-colour slip stitch) is a technique systematically documented by Barbara Walker in A Second Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1970), §Mosaic Patterns. The specific mosaic pattern used here is a simple Greek key variant that appears in Walker's mosaic section as a standard public domain geometric form.

glossaryTerms.definition: A two-colour slip-stitch technique invented by Barbara Walker where only one colour is worked per row. The other colour is slipped without working, creating a colourwork pattern from the slipped stitches reading through from previous rows. No stranding or carrying across the back.

glossaryTerms.term: Sl1 wyif (slip 1 with yarn in front)
glossaryTerms.definition: Slip the next stitch purlwise with the yarn held in front of the work. On garter fabric, this carries the yarn across the face of the slipped stitch as a horizontal bar.

content.text: A rectangular wrap in DK wool worked in
mosaic knitting
, a two-colour slip-stitch method where only one colour is worked per row. Finished size approximately 40 × 170 cm.

The mosaic method is significantly easier than stranded colourwork: there are no floats to manage across the WS and tension is entirely controlled by the single active colour. The Greek key mosaic pattern used here is an 8-stitch, 16-row repeat. Budget about 200 g (about 440 m / 480 yards) of each of two DK yarns in strongly contrasting values.
What you need

items.name: Colour A (light)
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn

items.name: Colour B (dark)
items.qty: About 200 g (440 m / 480 yards) of DK-weight yarn in a contrasting value

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 4 mm (UK 8 / US 6) needle, 50 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over mosaic pattern on 4 mm needles, unblocked. Do not wet-block mosaic fabric; it flattens the slip stitch texture. At gauge the 88-stitch cast-on gives a 40 cm width. If your gauge reads 24 stitches per 10 cm, cast on 96 stitches for a similar width.
Stitches used

items.name: wyib / wyif
items.qty: with yarn in back / with yarn in front

content.text: Pattern
Cast on
Using colour A and the long-tail cast-on, cast on 88 stitches (11 × 8-stitch repeats). Tail: approximately 50 cm.
Mosaic pattern (8 sts, 16 rows)
Colour A rows (RS then WS back): Row 1A (RS): *k6 A, sl1 wyib, k1 A; repeat from *. Row 2A (WS): *k1 A,
sl1 wyif
, k6 A; repeat from *.
Colour B rows: Row 3B (RS): *k2 B, sl1 wyib, k5 B; repeat from *. Row 4B (WS): *k5 B, sl1 wyif, k2 B; repeat from *.

Continue alternating colour pairs (2 rows A, 2 rows B) with the slip stitch position shifting 1 stitch per colour change to build the Greek key diagonal. Work all 16 rows of the repeat, then repeat the 16 rows until the wrap measures 170 cm. Both colours are attached at the same edge; bring the new colour up from the bottom when needed.
Bind off
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off in colour A after completing a full 16-row repeat.
Stitch count check-ins
Every 16-row repeat: stitch count must remain 88. Mosaic knitting never increases or decreases stitch count.
Common faults

Slipped stitches on wrong side of fabric: the yarn was brought in front for a wyib slip or to the back for a wyif slip. On a RS row, slipped stitches carry the yarn behind the work (wyib) so the colour bar lies on the RS. On a WS row, slipped stitches carry the yarn in front of the work (wyif) so the colour bar again lies on the RS of the fabric.
Motif diagonal not consistent: a colour was used for 4 rows instead of 2. Each colour pair is exactly 2 rows (RS + WS), then switch. Use a row counter.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water, roll in a towel to remove excess water, lay flat to dry. Do not wet-block: the mosaic structure depends on the slip-stitch texture remaining raised.
What to try next

A three-colour mosaic uses three colours in rotation (2 rows of each): colour A, colour B, colour C. The mosaic pattern positions the slipped stitches to build motifs from all three colours reading through successive rows.
